title: four owner-approved question defects (stimulation, wellcontrol, perfsand, hydraulics)

items.flag: the correct option said the pseudo-skin halves with the damage factor; it passes through the logarithmic Cinco-Ley and Samaniego correlation, so it does not
items.reason: correct option and explanation now say conductivity and dimensionless conductivity halve while the pseudo-skin worsens less than proportionally (engine fracDesign.js fracProductivity; halving the published case moves it from -5.31 to about -4.77)
items.correct_change_reason: owner 2026-09-21: the keyed statement was physically wrong

0.old: The conductivity, the dimensionless conductivity and the pseudo-skin all halve along with the factor.
0.new: Conductivity and dimensionless conductivity halve, and the pseudo-skin rises toward zero without halving.

explanation.old: Because it carries straight through, the factor should be quoted beside the answer rather than buried in the inputs.
explanation.new: The factor multiplies the retained permeability, so conductivity and dimensionless conductivity halve with it. The pseudo-skin passes through a logarithmic correlation, so it rises toward zero and does not halve. Quote the factor beside the answer.

items.flag: the explanation ended "so the shut-in limit is generous", which contradicts the keyed shut-in case (lesson m02 l04: on the slant well the shut-in case binds)
items.reason: explanation rewritten to the lesson mechanism; key and options unchanged

explanation.old: A large gap means the influx can be tall at the bottom before the shoe notices, so the shut-in limit is generous.
explanation.new: A large gap lets the influx rise and expand a long way before its top reaches the shoe, so the circulated case comes out the larger. The shut-in headroom is the tighter limit, and the smaller case wins.

items.flag: the prompt asked what happens to a thirty degree phasing while the options list four conditions and the explanation classifies result, warning and null
items.reason: prompt now asks which condition the engine refuses outright (lesson m01 l04 "What it will refuse"); explanation names why; key unchanged

prompt.old: Somebody enters a thirty degree phasing. What happens, and why?
prompt.new: Which of these does the engine refuse outright, where the others come back as a result, a warning or a null?

explanation.old: A positive skin is a result, an out-of-range group is a warning, and a short sieve returns nulls.
explanation.new: A phasing outside the six published angles, thirty degrees for one, is refused. A positive skin is a result, an out-of-range group is a warning, and a short sieve returns nulls.

items.flag: the explanation said "The first is the one the whole next tier is built on", but option 0 in stored order is the bit square law and the key is option 2
items.reason: explanation now names the keyed idea instead of an order reference (lesson m06 l03: the next tier is about the one loss that reaches the rock)

explanation.old: All three are true. The first is the one the whole next tier is built on.
explanation.new: All four are true of this system. Only the annulus loss reaches the rock, and the next tier is about what the rock feels.
